Why do we light lamps on the day before Diwali? As the story goes, a demon king named Narakasura stole the earrings of the mother of the gods, and locked away sixteen thousand princesses.
Krishna flew out on his eagle, Garuda, to stop him. And next to him, holding a bow, sat his queen, Satyabhama. The battle was fierce. Krishna fell, wounded, for a moment.
Wait, who saved the day? Satyabhama. She drew her bow, and with one arrow, Narakasura fell. The princesses were free. And the people lit lamps all through the night.
That's why the day before Diwali is called Naraka Chaturdashi. Light wins over darkness. Comment Satyabhama, for the queen who fought.
